title: Lipo Foam and Boards: What They Do, How Long to Wear Them
meta_description: Lipo foam is a soft layer worn under your compression garment after liposuction. What foam and boards do, how to wear them, skin care and when to stop.
excerpt: Lipo foam is a soft sheet worn on the skin under your compression garment after liposuction, and boards add a firm layer on top. Here is what each does, how to wear them, how to protect your skin and why your surgeon sets how long.
quick_answer:
What is lipo foam?

Lipo foam is a soft, flexible foam sheet worn directly on the skin under your compression garment after liposuction, to spread pressure evenly and cushion seams and creases. The Aesthetic Society says the garment itself is worn for 4 to 6 weeks; how long you wear foam and boards is your surgeon's call.

sources.title: Liposuction aftercare and recovery
quotes: You will wear a compression garment over the treated areas for four to six weeks to control swelling and promote skin contraction.
The swelling will peak around 48 hours after surgery and will mostly disappear within two to three weeks, but there may be slight residual swelling for up to four months.
Your incisions may be leaky or drain fluids for several days.

sources.title: Use of Reston foam in liposuction (Schlesinger SL, Kaczynski AJ, 1993;17(1):49-51, PMID 8430530)
quotes: Use of Reston foam along with a pressure garment after liposuction results in three salutary effects: less waviness in the skin surface, a more comfortable recovery, and less blood loss and ecchymoses.
In addition, the use of the foam, in conjunction with the pressure garment, results in less postoperative bleeding and bruising.

sources.title: A new foam girdle for the significant reduction of ecchymoses post-liposuction (Brandy DA, 2002;28(12):1135-7, PMID 12472493)
quotes: This garment is kept on for two to three days.

In most cases, Reston foam is a good adjunct to liposuction surgery. However, it can occasionally cause allergic dermatitis, bullae formation or postinflammatory hyper-pigmentation and can take an inordinately long time to apply.

sources.publisher: Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Global Open (PubMed; full text via Europe PMC PMC10519563)
sources.title: The Use of Postoperative Compression Garments in Plastic Surgery—Necessary or Not? A Practical Review (Ormseth BH and colleagues, 2023;11(9):e5293)
quotes: Although plastic surgeons have frequently reported the use of compression garments after body contouring operations,43–45 no RCTs or comparative studies have been conducted to evaluate the efficacy of compression in this setting.
In 2006, he noted how excessive or poorly distributed compression could result in venous stasis and thrombosis along with skin folding and bulging.

sources.title: Eight ways to make liposuction recovery a breeze (Kaitlin Clark, August 4, 2022)
quotes: He advises his liposuction patients to wear a customized compression garment for four to eight weeks, while patients whose procedure included athletic sculpting, will also be given a supplemental foam to place under the garment.
